plants.name: Hippeastrum x hybridum
plants.description: Towering stems carry trumpet-shaped blooms up to 8 inches wide. They glow like festive lanterns on windowsills while winter settles in outside.
plants.bloomingSeason: Late autumn to late winter when forced indoors in the Northern Hemisphere (typically December to February); outdoors in the Southern Hemisphere, flowering peaks in spring to early summer (October to December).
plants.location: Indoors across North America and Europe; outdoors in warm-climate gardens such as Australia and South Africa
plants.funFact: Amaryllis bulbs are often sold waxed or in kits that bloom with no soil. The bulb stores enough energy to flower on its own.

plants.name: Camellia japonica
plants.description: Glossy evergreen shrubs burst into rose-like blooms with golden stamens in the cool of winter. Their flowers brighten gardens when little else is in flower.
plants.bloomingSeason: Late autumn through early spring, with many cultivars flowering from December to March
plants.location: Gardens in the southeastern United States, the Pacific Northwest, the UK, and Japan
plants.funFact: Tea comes from a close relative, Camellia sinensis. Camellia japonica seed oil has long been used in Japan for hair care and cooking.

plants.name: Metrosideros excelsa
plants.description: Coastal trees erupt in crimson pom-pom flowers made of hundreds of bright stamens. They paint cliffs and beaches red at the height of the Southern Hemisphere summer.
plants.bloomingSeason: Late spring to midsummer in New Zealand, peaking in December and early January
plants.funFact: The tree clings to sea cliffs with its roots and is a New Zealand symbol of the holiday season. Its flowering time is why it is called the Christmas tree there.
